## TL;DR

Review pass 6: the `validate.sh` completed-capture startup sweep now emits `[reaper] removed …` only after `docker rm -f` and the container is gone, and `[reaper] failed to remove … reason=…` when removal fails. `recordValidateStartupReapedCaptures` maps failures to warn/infra task events. Earlier passes already added shared collection/reaping on both providers. Handoff tree: local HEAD at commit time of this draft.

## Work and rationale

Reporting success before removal was observability debt: the Mac parser treated any reaper-shaped line as success even if the container survived. The shell block now captures `rm_out` and `rm_code`, verifies the id is gone on success, and never prints “removed” on failure. Failures stay on the validate stream (stdout) so the existing SSH emit path can parse them.

The non-running startup sweep (`xargs docker rm`) remains silent and best-effort — it does not emit success markers, so there is no false-success path there.

## Approaches tried

Kept `[reaper]` as a distinct prefix from `[validate] gate exit` so log parsing stays unambiguous. Extended `newlySeenValidateFailedReapCaptures` with an exported parser test rather than scraping full integration output.

## Challenges and blockers

Live runner confirmation on thinkpad/bee/mini remains human-owned; unit tests cover marker order, parse rules, and event levels.

## Key learnings

Any host-side cleanup that drives Debug events must couple markers to command outcomes, not intentions. A suppressed `|| true` on `docker rm` is fine for liveness; claiming success is not.
